candidates.exact_span:
Citations to 40 CFR are as of December 6, 2013.
Sections 122, 124, 125, 133, 136
candidates.computation_change_reason: The as-of date fixes which edition of federal regulations grounds the permit; cited Parts 125 and 133 bear on effluent and water-quality-based numeric limit derivation (A), while Parts 122 and 124 bear on permit terms and monitoring program requirements (B). A different reading of the snapshot date or which parts are incorporated could change which federal limit and monitoring frameworks are treated as authoritative for FY2025 evaluation.

candidates.exact_span:
New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Water, 20.6.4 NMAC,
effective, effective July 24, 2020.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This cites the state surface-water quality standards rule and its effective date as an administrative-record basis for the permit. Interpreting which NMAC version applies—or whether these standards supply the numeric limits used for compliance comparison—could change which enforceable discharge limits are selected for FY2025 measurements.

candidates.exact_span:
Procedures for Implementing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Permits in New
Mexico, March 15, 2012.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This references state NPDES implementation procedures as a basis for the proposed permit. Different interpretation of whether and how these procedures define monitoring frequency, conditional requirements, or event-driven obligations could change which monitoring requirements are treated as applicable during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: State of New Mexico 303(d) List for Assessed Stream and River Reaches, 2014 - 2016.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cited 303(d) list vintage identifies which impaired-water listing was used in permit development. Interpreting whether this listing triggers additional water-quality-based limits (A) or supplemental/impairment-driven monitoring obligations (B) for the permitted discharge could change FY2025 limit selection and monitoring-applicability results.
